paper_title: Simple mathematical models with very complicated dynamics
focus: Apply x_next = r*x*(1-x) repeatedly, using each output as the next input. Display the initial state and four updates. This short trajectory demonstrates recurrence, without claiming to establish chaos. Choose complete numerical checks at exactly representable states r=4,x0=0.5 and r=2,x0=0.5, checking named first and fourth updates. The trajectory visualization includes the initial state plus all four updates, hence five values.
excerpt:
Simple mathematical models with very complicated dynamics. Robert M. May (1976). Section 2, equation (3), Caltech/NED reprint.
This is sometimes called the "logistic" difference equation.
Equation transcription: X_(t+1) = a*X_t*(1-X_t). Modern teaching notation renames a to r: x_next = r*x*(1-x). The teaching experiment includes x in [0,1] and r in [0,4], displaying only four successive updates.
